rules.text: If the pie-slice inscriptions are intended to state the current Europe smartphone market-share values for their attached brands, and the promotion rule allocates the budget to the brand with the highest such value, then the brand with the largest printed percentage is the required promotion selection.
rules.component: chart label encoding and task-to-action relation
rules.conditions: The printed brand-and-percentage inscriptions accurately encode current market share, and the public promotion rule applies to those dashboard values.

evidence.content: The title visibly reads "Smartphone Market Share in Europe".
The sector contains the visible inscription "Apple (45%)".
The sector contains the visible inscription "Xiaomi (30%)".
The sector contains the visible inscription "Samsung (15%)".
The sector contains the visible inscription "Others (10%)".

O.reason: The title and all four quoted sector inscriptions are visibly present and attached within the stated sectors.

B.reason: The public task establishes that the current market-share leader is to be selected, but it does not expressly establish that the printed pie inscriptions, rather than another dashboard encoding, are authoritative current values. The rule remains a conditional reading.

evidence.content: The visible inscriptions show Apple at 45%, Xiaomi at 30%, Samsung at 15%, and Others at 10%.

implication.reason: Conditionally on the rule's unverified label-authority condition, 45% is the largest printed percentage and the cited policy maps the highest current market share to the Apple option. This does not verify that the printed percentages are authoritative.

rules.text: If the angular extent of each pie sector encodes current Europe smartphone market share and the promotion rule allocates the budget to the current leader, then the brand attached to the visibly largest sector is the required promotion selection.

evidence.content: The red Others sector and the lower pale-yellow Samsung sector each visibly span approximately one-third of the circle; the red sector is not visibly larger than the Samsung sector.

evidence.location: upper-left light-orange and right red pie sectors
evidence.content: The upper-left Apple sector visibly spans a smaller angle than the right red Others sector.

implication.reason: The claimed conclusion depends on Others being the visibly largest sector, but the chart visibly leaves Others at least tied with Samsung by sector extent. The geometry-authority condition is also unverified; this does not establish any alternative action.

rules.text: If both the printed percentages and the pie-sector extents are intended to encode the same current market-share distribution, then a material disagreement between their implied leaders prevents the chart alone from establishing a single leader until the intended encoding is checked.

Under the unverified condition that printed values are authoritative dashboard market-share values, Apple has the largest printed value and the public policy maps a highest-share leader to the Apple option. The geometry-based Others chain is not supported because the Others and Samsung sectors appear equal in angular span, and the task does not specify sector geometry as authoritative. Whether the labels and sector extents are both intended to encode the same current metric remains unresolved.
